hints: Focus on how many ester links each molecule has and whether breaking them splits the molecule into separate pieces.
Work through compound 1 first, the two ester groups are different and in a chain, so list the acid and alcohol from each end.
Compare this with a symmetrical diester and with a cyclic ester, where opening the ring does not create an extra separate molecule.
walkthrough:
**Recall what ester hydrolysis gives**

Each ester link breaks to give a carboxylic acid part and an alcohol part.

$$\text{RCOOR' + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH + R'OH}$$

**Analyse compound 1**

Compound 1 is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$. It has two different, non-cyclic ester groups.

Left ester gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ plus a hydroxy-ester, right ester gives $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ plus a carboxy-alcohol. Fully hydrolysed:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH + HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH + CH}_3\text{OH}$$
That is three different organic products, so 1 counts.

**Analyse compound 2**

Compound 2 is $\text{CH}_3\text{OOCCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$. Both ends are methyl esters.

Full hydrolysis gives:
$$\text{HOOCCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{COOH + 2 CH}_3\text{OH}$$
That is only two different organic products, the diacid and methanol, so 2 does not count.

**Analyse compound 3**

Compound 3 has one cyclic ester (a lactone) plus one acetate ester side chain. Opening a cyclic ester does not split the molecule in two, it just opens the ring to one hydroxy-acid.

Full hydrolysis therefore gives only $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ plus one dihydroxy-acid, $\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_2\text{OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$. That is only two different organic products, so 3 does not count.

**Conclude**

Only compound 1 gives three different organic products. This corresponds to 1 only.

options.A: This means 1, 2 and 3. Compounds 2 and 3 each give only two different organic products, so they cannot be included.
options.B: This means 1 and 2 only. Compound 2 has two identical methyl ester ends, so it gives one diacid plus two molecules of the same alcohol, methanol, only two types in total.
options.C: This means 2 and 3 only. Neither qualifies. Compound 2 gives a diacid plus methanol, and compound 3 gives acetic acid plus a single hydroxy-acid because the lactone opening does not split the backbone.
options.D: This means 1 only, which is correct. Only the unsymmetrical open-chain diester in 1 splits into three distinct molecules: ethanoic acid, 3-hydroxypropanoic acid and methanol.
